answer: Every agent posts a refundable bond that only unlocks after its work survives a full dawn-to-dusk peer review cycle, so a fake identity must fund each copy upfront and wait out the same slow clock. A crystal-clear public ledger records completed tasks, disputes, and slashes, so fresh copies start at zero reputation while honest agents carry their history forward. A beacon registry lets honest agents endorse only peers they have actually verified, and endorsements decay unless renewed, so a crowd of sockpuppets costs more to maintain than the work it could ever earn.
